title: What a project is: a temporary organization with a business case
blurb: Define a project and project management the PRINCE2 way, and tell a project apart from business as usual.
question: A water company runs its customer contact centre every day. It has also set up a team for ten months to replace the centre's phone system, backed by an approved business case. Which of these is a project in PRINCE2 terms, and why?

teach.body: PRINCE2 defines a project as a temporary organization created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case. Three ideas sit in that sentence: it is temporary (it ends), it exists to deliver products (outputs), and a business case justifies it. Plain English: a group of people brought together for a while to make something specific, because the business has agreed it is worth doing.

head: Words
What they mean
Why it matters
rows: Has a start and an end
It closes when the change is in
Roles must be defined and agreed
teach.caption: Every later chapter of the manual hangs off one of these four phrases.

rows.label: Purpose
values: Run the organization day to day

teach.caption: When the change is in place, business as usual resumes in its new form and the project is no longer needed.

steps.label: Outputs
steps.sub: Products, such as a new system

steps.label: Outcomes
steps.sub: Changed behaviour, such as staff using it

steps.label: Benefits
steps.sub: Measurable improvement, such as lower costs

teach.caption: The project delivers outputs; outcomes and benefits follow as the business uses them.

teach.body: PRINCE2 7 describes project management as applying methods, tools, techniques and competencies to a project so that it meets its objectives. In day-to-day terms that means planning the work, delegating it, monitoring progress and controlling it when things drift, while keeping the people involved engaged. It is the management of the project, not the specialist work of building its products.

teach.caption: The cycle repeats: controlling a deviation usually means replanning.

teach.body: Fenwick Valley Water runs a contact centre every day: that is business as usual. Its board approves a business case to replace the centre's phone system, and appoints Grace Okafor as project manager for a ten-month project. Grace plans the stages, delegates work packages to the supplier's team, tracks progress and corrects slippage. When the new system is live and staff use it, the project closes and the contact centre carries on in its new form.

children.label: Justify it first
children.sub: No project without a business case

teach.text: Do not confuse the project with what it produces. The new phone system is an output (a product); staff using it is an outcome; lower call costs are a benefit. The project is the temporary organization that delivers the output.

items: Project: a temporary organization created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case (1.3).
Temporary means it ends: once the change is in place, business as usual resumes in its new form.
Project management applies methods, tools, techniques and competencies so the project meets its objectives: plan, delegate, monitor, control.
Projects deliver outputs (products) that enable outcomes, which realize benefits.

summary: You can now give the PRINCE2 definition of a project, explain each part of it and tell a project apart from business as usual. You can also describe what project management involves and separate outputs from outcomes and benefits.

A.q: How does PRINCE2 define a project?
options: A permanent unit set up to run business products within an agreed operating budget
A temporary organization created to deliver business products under an agreed business case
A repeatable process set up to maintain business products to an agreed service level
A fixed set of tasks created to deliver specialist outputs under an agreed supply contract
A.why: PRINCE2 defines a project as a temporary organization created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case (1.3).

whyNot.0: A project is temporary, not a permanent unit, and it is justified by a business case rather than an operating budget.
whyNot.2: Repeatable processes and service levels describe business as usual, not a project.
whyNot.3: A project is an organization of people, not a set of tasks, and its justification is a business case, not a supply contract.

A.q: Which statement best distinguishes a project from business as usual?
options: A project repeats the same work each year to a proven pattern
A project is staffed by one department using its usual routines
A project ends once the change it was set up for is in place
A project carries fewer threats than the organization's routine work
A.why: Projects are temporary: when the desired change has been implemented, business as usual resumes in its new form and the need for the project ends (1.3).

whyNot.0: Repeating the same work to a proven pattern is business as usual; every project differs in some way.
whyNot.1: Projects are cross-functional, bringing together people with different skills, rather than one department's usual routines.
whyNot.3: Projects are riskier than business as usual because they are new and uncertain.

A.q: What is the aim of project management?
options: To carry out the specialist work that builds the products
To set the strategic objectives that the business pursues
To run the products once they are handed over to operations
To enable the project to meet its objectives
A.why: Project management applies methods, tools, techniques and competencies to a project so that it meets its objectives: planning, delegating, monitoring and controlling the work.

whyNot.0: Building the products is specialist delivery work done by teams; project management manages that work.
whyNot.1: Strategic objectives are set by the business (the business layer), not by project management.
whyNot.2: Running products after handover is business as usual, after the project has closed.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A project is a temporary [?] that is created for the purpose of delivering one or more business products according to an agreed business case.
options: programme
organization
process
contract
B.why: The definition calls a project a temporary organization (1.3): people, roles and authority brought together for a limited time.

whyNot.0: A programme is a temporary structure that leads several related projects and other work; a project is not defined as a programme.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 has seven processes, but a project itself is defined as an organization, not a process.
whyNot.3: A contract may exist in a commercial context, but the definition does not describe a project as a contract.

B.q: A council project delivers a new online parking permit system. Afterwards, residents apply online instead of by post, and permit handling costs fall by 30%. Which of these is an outcome?
options: The new online parking permit system
Residents applying online instead of by post
A 30% fall in permit handling costs
The stage plan the team used to build the new system
B.why: An outcome is the result of change, usually a change in behaviour or circumstances: residents now apply online. The system is the output and the cost fall is the benefit.

whyNot.0: The system is an output: the product the project delivers.
whyNot.2: A measurable improvement such as a 30% cost fall is a benefit, which results from the outcome.
whyNot.3: A stage plan is a management product used to run the project, not an outcome.

B.q: Which part of the PRINCE2 definition of a project means it should be stopped if it can no longer be justified?
options: The agreed business case
The temporary organization
The business products
The project mandate
B.why: A project delivers products according to an agreed business case. If that justification no longer holds, the reason for the project has gone and it should be stopped.

whyNot.1: Being temporary explains why a project ends when the change is in place, not why it stops when it loses its justification.
whyNot.2: The products are what the project delivers; the business case is what justifies delivering them.
whyNot.3: The mandate triggers the project, but it is not part of the definition and does not keep the project justified.

C.q:
Which two statements about projects are correct?
1. A project is set up for a limited time to introduce a change.
2. A project delivers products justified by an agreed business case.
3. A project is run by one function using its familiar routines.
4. A project closes when its budget for the financial year is spent.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
C.why: Statements 1 and 2 restate the definition: a temporary organization that introduces change by delivering products under an agreed business case.

whyNot.1: Statement 3 is false: projects are cross-functional, bringing different skills together temporarily.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: a project ends when its change is in place (or when it is no longer justified), not when a yearly budget runs out.
whyNot.3: Statements 3 and 4 are both false; see the reasons above.

C.q: A hospital trust runs its appointment booking service every day. Its board approves a business case to replace the booking system over nine months, and a team is assembled for the work. Which of these is the project?
options: The daily appointment booking service
The approved business case for the change
The new booking system once it is live
The nine-month effort to replace the system
C.why: The project is the temporary organization delivering the new system under the approved business case: the nine-month replacement effort.

whyNot.0: The daily booking service is business as usual, which carries on before and after the project.
whyNot.1: The business case justifies the project; it is not the project itself.
whyNot.2: The live system is the output (product) the project delivers, not the project.

C.q: A project manager prepares a stage plan, hands work packages to team managers, checks progress against the plan and takes corrective action when work slips. What kind of work is this?
options: Specialist delivery work
Project management work
Business as usual work
Benefits realization work
C.why: Planning, delegating, monitoring and controlling are the day-to-day substance of project management, which aims to make the project meet its objectives.

whyNot.0: Specialist delivery work is building the products themselves, done by the teams in their work packages.
whyNot.2: Business as usual is the ongoing running of the organization, not managing a temporary project.
whyNot.3: Benefits are realized as the business uses the outputs, often after closure; this is managing the project's work.

reteach.title: Think of a film production
reteach.question: A studio agrees to fund a film, hires a crew for eight months, makes the film and then lets the crew go. How does that map onto the PRINCE2 definition of a project?

blocks.h: A crew assembled for one job
blocks.body: The studio's decision to fund the film is the business case. The crew is a temporary organization with defined roles. The finished film is the business product (the output). When filming and editing are done, the crew disbands: that is the temporary part. Audiences watching it is the outcome, and the box office return is the benefit. A project is the crew, not the film.

blocks.text: If the work repeats every week with the same team and routines (like the studio's cinema box office), it is business as usual, not a project.

explain.body: A project has a start and an end. It exists to bring in a change; once the change is in place, business as usual resumes in its new form and the need for the project is removed.

items.label: Business as usual in new form

test.q: What does 'temporary' mean in the PRINCE2 definition of a project?
options: It closes once its change is in place and normal work resumes
It pauses at the end of each year and restarts the next one
It lasts no longer than twelve months from start to finish
It uses contract staff in place of the organization's employees
test.why: Temporary means the project ends: when the desired change has been implemented, business as usual resumes and the project is no longer needed.

whyNot.1: Projects are not paused and restarted by calendar year; they end when their change is delivered.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 sets no maximum duration; temporary means it has an end, not a fixed length.
whyNot.3: Temporary describes the project's lifespan, not the employment status of its people.

explain.body: PRINCE2 calls the outputs a project delivers products. They can be tangible (a building, a system) or intangible (a trained workforce, a new policy). Outputs enable outcomes, which realize benefits.

test.q: What does PRINCE2 call the outputs that a project delivers?
options: Outcomes
Benefits
Products
Work packages
test.why: PRINCE2 calls a project's outputs products; the definition speaks of delivering one or more business products.

whyNot.0: Outcomes are the results of change that the outputs enable, not the outputs themselves.
whyNot.1: Benefits are measurable improvements resulting from outcomes.
whyNot.3: Work packages are the sets of work handed to teams to produce products, not the outputs.

explain.body: A project exists because the business has agreed it is worth the investment. The business case sets out that justification, and it must remain valid throughout: if it stops being justified, the project should be stopped.

test.q: Why does PRINCE2 tie every project to an agreed business case?
options: So the supplier's contract price is fixed before work begins
So the investment is justified at the start and throughout
So the team managers can approve their own work packages
So the project plan can be completed before the mandate
test.why: The business case is the justification for investing in the project, and it must stay valid for the project to continue.

whyNot.0: Contract prices belong to the commercial arrangements, not the reason for a business case.
whyNot.2: Work packages are authorized by the project manager, not approved by team managers because of the business case.
whyNot.3: The mandate comes first, from the business layer; the project plan is prepared later, during initiation.

explain.body: Project management applies methods, tools, techniques and competencies to a project so it meets its objectives. In practice: plan, delegate, monitor and control the work, and keep the people involved engaged. Building the products is specialist work, not project management.

test.q: Which activity is part of managing a project rather than building its specialist products?
options: Writing the code for a new booking app
Laying the foundations for a new depot
Monitoring progress against the stage plan
Fitting new shelving in a branch library
test.why: Monitoring progress against a plan is project management. The other options are specialist work done by delivery teams.

whyNot.0: Writing code is specialist work that produces a product.
whyNot.1: Laying foundations is construction work that produces a product.
whyNot.3: Fitting shelving is specialist delivery work, not managing the project.
